---
title: "History"
subtitle: "From institutional and agency support toward CSIL"
---

This section follows the development of ideas and arrangements that preceded the named CSIL program, then traces its early years and later evolution.

The sequence is useful for reading the evidence, but it is **not** a claim that one project formally became the next. The surviving record does not show that Creekview became ECPM, or that ECPM formally became CSIL.

## The story in brief

**Before CSIL**, many people with high physical support needs lived in institutions such as Pearson Hospital or received limited hours of support through agencies. Through the 1970s and early 1980s, disabled people and community-living advocates tested other arrangements. That earlier context is summarized in the [Creekview](creekview.qmd) chapter.

**[Creekview](creekview.qmd) (c. 1984–89)** was a Vancouver co-op where six men with high-level, mostly ventilator-dependent quadriplegia moved out of hospital. Contemporary and near-contemporary sources describe a resident-and-Canadian Paraplegic Association project that depended on government agreement and public funding. Creekview did not create CSIL, and the evidence does not show a CSIL-style individual employer contract. It did demonstrate that people with very high support needs could live outside an institution and exercise some control over their daily support.

**[Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM)](ecpm.qmd) (c. 1990)** appears in a bibliography as the title of a training manual intended to help consumers act as employers. The manual itself has not yet been found. Later organizations also use ECPM to describe an individual-funding project that preceded CSIL. Whether those references describe exactly the same initiative remains unresolved.

**[CSIL design and pilot](csil-pilot.qmd).** By late 1995, a Ministry of Health program publicly named Choice in Supports for Independent Living existed. Later official records describe a 1994 pilot and province-wide availability in 1995. Other later accounts use 1993 or 1994 as an establishment date, while a 1995 union newspaper still described CSIL as new or a pilot. The chapter therefore does not select a single founding year.

**[Later evolution](evolution.qmd) (2008 onward)** follows a more established program through the 2008 program review, later rate changes, and current definitions such as client support group and CSIL representative. Those later rules should not be read backward as proof of how the program operated in the 1990s.

The [timeline](../timeline.qmd) places the working dates in sequence. The [sources catalogue](../sources/index.qmd) holds the underlying records.

## What the evidence shows — and what it does not {#state-of-the-evidence}

### Well established

- Creekview existed as a mid-1980s community residence for a small group of men with high-level, mostly ventilator-dependent quadriplegia. It was planned by February 1984 and in place by April 1986 ([Creekview](creekview.qmd)).
- A 1990 ECPM *Skill Development Manual* from BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society is independently listed in a bibliography. The manual itself has not been read ([ECPM](ecpm.qmd)).
- By late 1995, a Ministry of Health program publicly named Choice in Supports for Independent Living existed. A contemporary union newspaper described it as new or a pilot ([HEU *Guardian* Nov/Dec 1995](../sources/1995-heu-guardian-novdec.qmd)).
- A November 2008 CSIL Program Review Synthesis Report exists and has been read from an Internet Archive Microlog fiche.
- Current ministry policy defines CSIL employer, client support group, and CSIL representative ([HCC Policy 4.C](../sources/hcc-policy-manual-4c.qmd)). These are current rules, not recovered 1990s records.

### Later accounts

Later sources add important detail but are not records from the events themselves. They include:

- SCI BC and journalistic accounts of Creekview and the people associated with it
- IFRC and Paul Gauthier materials describing ECPM as a step before CSIL and using 1993 or 1994 establishment dates
- the 2012 Ombudsperson report describing a **1994 pilot** and **1995 province-wide availability**
- the Order of Canada citation describing Paul Gauthier as an “Initiator” of CSIL

### Still unresolved

- whether there was any formal succession from Creekview to ECPM to CSIL
- the full text of the 1990 ECPM manual, and whether a separate 1994 version existed
- *Keys on Freedom*, whose title, author and year remain unconfirmed
- original 1993–95 Ministry of Health design and pilot records
- a single founding year for CSIL
- the 1987 Creekview evaluation report
- whether the Ombudsperson's reference to a 2007 provincial review is the same work as the November 2008 synthesis
